maya (SRE): noticing a P99 latency regression starting ~06:12 UTC, concurrent with several GPU OOMs on inference-prod-gpu-1 pool. raising a thread to collect logs and decide mitigation.
jonathan (runtime): can you paste the p95/p99 times and any recent deploys? also which models affected?
maya (SRE): p95 ~ 240ms -> 260ms (small), p99 spiked 1.1s -> 3.8s. Affected routes: /v1/completions (gpt-like), /v1/chat. No deploys in last 3 hours per deploy-bot. Models: redwood-open-7b-qlora and rdx-vicuna-13b.
eli (support): a customer opened a ticket complaining timeouts at ~06:30 UTC. correlates.
sophia (ml-eng): any signs of KV cache growth? ive seen p99 regressions when kv_cache keeps growing per session.
maya (SRE): logs from one impacted node attached below. root cause looks like repeated OOM kills of the model process with slow restarts and memory fragmentation.
maya (SRE): ```
# from node inference-prod-gpu-1a
nvidia-smi --query-gpu=timestamp,name,utilization.gpu,memory.used,memory.total --format=csv -l 60 | tail -n 5
2026-03-15 06:11:20, NVIDIA A100, 87 %, 38231 MiB, 40536 MiB
2026-03-15 06:12:20, NVIDIA A100, 92 %, 39988 MiB, 40536 MiB
2026-03-15 06:13:20, NVIDIA A100, 99 %, 40480 MiB, 40536 MiB
```
maya (SRE): and from the runtime logs (truncated):
maya (SRE): ```
[06:12:15] runtime] session_id=abc123 kv_cache_entries=524288 kv_cache_bytes=3.2G
[06:12:18] runtime] GPU OOM: failed to allocate 120MB for attention_kv
[06:12:18] kernel] oom-killer invoked: kill process 4567 (model-serving)
[06:12:19] runtime] restarting model-serving pid=4567 -> 7890 (took 900ms)
[06:12:19] runtime] recovered, rebuilding KV cache for session abc123
[06:12:25] runtime] defragmentation attempt=1 result=insufficient
```
jonathan (runtime): kv_cache_entries=524k and 3.2GB of kv is worrying. That explains fragmentation + OOM. Which allocator are we on? jemalloc or tcmalloc?
sophia (ml-eng): runtime uses custom allocator on CUDA + CUDAMallocCaching (a small internal caching allocator) + host-side jemalloc. CUDA caching can fragment badly if many variable-length kvs.
eli (support): any quick mitigations we can tell customers while we fix infra?
maya (SRE): immediate mitigations I propose:
- limit kv_cache entries per session (soft cap 64k)
- enable kv eviction policy LRU-approx and background reclaim every 30s
- tune CUDA caching allocator to release >50MB free blocks back to device (tunable param "cuda_cache_min_free")
- rolling restart of 3 nodes in inference-prod-gpu-1 to defragment
jonathan (runtime): agree. quick patch: set KV_MAX_ENTRIES=65536 and KV_EVICT_RATE=0.05 in runtime config. Also enable runtime flag --cuda-cache-min-free-mb=64.
sophia (ml-eng): will that impact latency negatively due to more misses? might increase token compute slightly but better than repeated OOMs.
maya (SRE): scheduling a rolling restart. will patch config via infra's config-service and then roll 3 nodes with 5m spacing. patch commands below:
maya (SRE): ```
# patch config (kubectl patch equivalent)
kubectl set env cm/inference-runtime KV_MAX_ENTRIES=65536 KV_EVICT_RATE=0.05 --namespace=prod
# runtime flag update for helm values
--set runtime.cudaCache.minFreeMb=64
```
deploy-bot: config change applied to config-service at 06:22:10 UTC by maya. rolling restart queued for pool inference-prod-gpu-1.
infra-bot: rolling restart started for inference-prod-gpu-1 (3 nodes) at 06:23:30 UTC.
jonathan (runtime): I also pushed a small change to the runtime to periodically call cudaMallocTrim (or equivalent) after N evictions to mitigate fragmentation. it's in canary: rtx-runtime:20260315-evict-trim. No restart yet.
eli (support): told customer we are investigating OOM-related latency and applying mitigations; asked them to retry in 20 minutes. :hourglass_flowing_sand:
sophia (ml-eng): note: KV growth patterns show long-lived sessions with long context windows causing explosion. we should add session TTLs and enforce max_context_tokens per session in the longer term.
maya (SRE): first node restarted at 06:29:40, second at 06:35:05, third at 06:41:10. monitoring p95/p99.
eli (support): customer reports some immediate improvement but still seeing high p99 for a subset of requests.
maya (SRE): metrics update after first two restarts: p95 back to 250ms, p99 down to ~1.3s from 3.8s but still above baseline. after third restart + canary runtime trim enabled, p99 ~720ms.
jonathan (runtime): logs indicate fewer OOM kills post-change and KV sizes stabilized around 480MB per process after eviction policy. sample log:
jonathan (runtime): ```
[06:45:12] runtime] session_id=abc123 kv_cache_entries=40210 kv_cache_bytes=498M
[06:45:12] runtime] eviction: removed 1200 entries, reclaimed 84MB
[06:45:12] runtime] cuda_trim: freed 128MB device blocks
```
sophia (ml-eng): nice. we should roll the runtime patch to all nodes once canary is green and schedule a follow-up to add session TTLs and telemetry for per-session kv growth.
maya (SRE): action items before close:
- [x] patch KV_MAX_ENTRIES and KV_EVICT_RATE (done)
- [x] set cuda cache min free (done)
- [x] rolling restart of pool (done)
- [x] enable canary runtime trim (canary healthy)
- [ ] roll runtime patch globally (jonathan)
- [ ] add per-session TTL and telemetry (sophia)
- [ ] create runbook entry for GPU fragmentation + KV growth (maya)
eli (support): I updated the customer ticket with status and ETA for full rollout. will keep them updated.
jonathan (runtime): I'll start the global rollout after 15:00 UTC once we confirm no regressions in canary.
maya (SRE): monitoring for 2 hours; setting incident status to monitoring. thanks all. :white_check_mark:
